content.text:
[workspace]
resolver = "2"
exclude = ["tree-sitter-crepus"]
members = [
    "crates/crepuscularity",
    "crates/crepuscularity-core",
    "crates/crepuscularity-lsp",
    "crates/crepuscularity-native",
    "crates/crepuscularity-embedded",
    "crates/crepuscularity-embedded-macros",
    "crates/crepuscularity-lvgl",
    "crates/crepuscularity-abi",
    "crates/crepuscularity-gpui",
    "crates/crepuscularity-web",
    "crates/crepuscularity-webext",
    "crates/crepuscularity_macros",
    "crates/crepuscularity-runtime",
    "crates/crepuscularity-dev",
    "crates/crepuscularity-cli",
    "crates/crepuscularity-reactive",
    "crates/crepuscularity-ssr",
    "crates/crepuscularity-tui",
    # GPUI desktop shell with embedded V8 runtime (build V8 on demand):
    #   cargo build -p crepuscularity-lite
    #   cargo check --workspace --exclude crepuscularity-lite
    "crates/crepuscularity-lite",
    "examples/text-features",
    "examples/weather",
    "examples/todo",
    "examples/embedded-dashboard",
    "examples/embedded-stm32/host-sim",
    "examples/lvgl-pro-mode",
    "examples/lvgl-stm32",
]

[profile.release]
lto = "fat"
codegen-units = 1
panic = "abort"
strip = "symbols"

# ABI / cdylib embedders: `cargo build -p crepuscularity-abi --profile abi`
[profile.abi]
inherits = "release"
panic = "abort"
codegen-units = 1



# PGO-optimised release — use via scripts/pgo-build.sh:
#
#   scripts/pgo-build.sh pgo-gen   # step 1 & 2: instrumented build + profile run
#   scripts/pgo-build.sh pgo-use   # step 3:      rebuild with collected profiles
#
# Manual equivalent:
#   RUSTFLAGS="-Cprofile-generate=$(pwd)/target/pgo-profiles" \
#     cargo build --profile pgo -p crepuscularity-cli
#   # run crepus on a representative benchmark
#   RUSTFLAGS="-Cprofile-use=$(pwd)/target/pgo-profiles" \
#     cargo build --profile pgo -p crepuscularity-cli
[profile.pgo]
inherits = "release"
lto = "fat"
codegen-units = 1

[workspace.package]
version = "0.4.7"
edition = "2021"
license = "MPL-2.0"

# ── crepuscularity-lite workspace deps ────────────────────────────────────────
# These are only needed by crepuscularity-lite.
# Build with: cargo build -p crepuscularity-lite [--features cli]
# Check without V8: cargo check --workspace --exclude crepuscularity-lite

[workspace.dependencies]
# One requirement per external crate (loose semver). Run `cargo update` often;
# Cargo.lock records the exact versions used.
gpui = { version = "0.2.2", default-features = false, features = ["font-kit"] }
proc-macro2 = "1"
quote = "1"
syn = { version = "2", features = ["full", "extra-traits"] }
sha2 = "0.11"
toml = "1"
tracing = "0.1"
tracing-subscriber = { version = "0.3", features = ["env-filter"] }

axum = "0.8"
base64 = "0.22"
console = "0.16"
futures-util = "0.3"
http = "1"
indicatif = "0.18"
js-sys = "0.3"
notify = "8"
rayon = "1"
ratatui = "0.30"
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1"
tempfile = "3"
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["full"] }
tokio-stream = { version = "0.1", features = ["net"] }

# Crepuscularity

> **Stability:** This project is **unstable** and in active development. APIs, CLI flags, and template semantics may change without a semver-major release until **1.0**. Pin exact dependency versions and expect occasional breakage.

Think React Native turned into a systems UI toolkit: one compact `.crepus` language can drive GPUI desktop apps, Ratatui terminal UIs, Chromium/Firefox extensions, web output, native mobile shells, embedded panels, and LVGL Pro. Crepuscularity also ships hot reload, runtime rendering, and a GPUI desktop shell with an embedded V8 bridge for native capabilities.

Write UI in a concise, indentation-based template DSL (`.crepus` files). Templates compile at build time via the `view!` macro or render at runtime with full hot-reload support. The same `.crepus` syntax drives native desktop (GPUI), terminal UIs (Ratatui), browser extensions (MV3), HTML output, and React/JSX — and is the foundation for native mobile backends targeting SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose.

Use [Aurorality](https://github.com/tschk/aurorality) for united SwiftUI macOS + iOS apps.

## Why Crepuscularity

- **GPUI component workflow with hot reload** — live template updates without recompiling app code
- **Rust-owned MV3 extension target** — write popup, background, and content-script surfaces in `.crepus`, then emit Chromium or Firefox bundles without adopting a JavaScript framework or app bundler as the primary authoring model
- **One syntax, multiple backends** — the same template works across GPUI (native desktop), HTML, React/JSX, and browser extensions today; **`crepuscularity-native`** lowers `.crepus` to JSON **View IR** for SwiftUI / Jetpack Compose shells (see [`examples/native-shells`](examples/native-shells/README.md))
- **Polyglot plugin contract** — host languages consume View IR JSON through `crepus native ir` or the optional `crepuscularity-abi` C session API, then create UI from the typed node tree; drop-in reference packages and native workspace files live under [`plugins/`](plugins/README.md)
- **Terminal UIs without a second UI language** — **`crepuscularity-tui`** maps `.crepus` elements, includes, slots, control flow, and Tailwind-style terminal classes onto Ratatui frames
- **Embedded panels (in testing)** — **`crepuscularity-embedded`** renders `.crepus` into an RGB565 buffer you flush over SPI (**ILI9341**, **ST7789**) or into an **LTDC** framebuffer on STM32/ESP32; see [`docs/embedded.md`](docs/embedded.md) and [`examples/embedded-dashboard`](examples/embedded-dashboard/README.md)
- **Desktop shell for embedded guest apps** — **`crepuscularity-lite`** embeds V8 in a GPUI host with a Rust native-capability bridge, optional file watching, workers, plugin capabilities, and TypeScript/TSX guest transpilation
- **Compile-time and runtime paths** — `view!` macro for zero-overhead AOT compilation; `parse_template` / `render_nodes` for full runtime flexibility and hot reload

## Quick Start

```bash
# Install the CLI
cargo install --path crates/crepuscularity-cli

# If `crepus` is not found, Cargo still installed the binary under ~/.cargo/bin — add it to PATH,
# e.g. for zsh:  export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"
# (Rustup normally prepends this for login shells; some terminals omit it.)

# Create a new GPUI app
crepus init gpui my-app
cd my-app
SDKROOT=$(xcrun --show-sdk-path) cargo run

# Or create a browser extension
crepus init webext my-extension
cd my-extension
crepus build
# Load dist/unpacked/ in chrome://extensions
```

## Minimal target builds

Put every output in one `crepus.toml`, then run one command:

```toml
[[targets]]
type = "web"
id = "site"
site = "docs-site"
out = "docs-site/dist"
entry = "index.crepus"

[[targets]]
type = "lvgl"
id = "panel"
template = "ui.crepus"
out = "dist/panel.xml"
name = "Panel"
root = "screen"

[targets.vars]
device = "STM32F411"
```

```bash
crepus build
crepus build web
crepus build panel
crepus build --target panel
```

Rust build scripts can use the same manifest for render-output targets:

```rust
let artifacts = crepuscularity::target::write_manifest_file("crepus.toml")?;
```

    "crates/crepuscularity_macros",
    "crates/crepuscularity-runtime",
    "crates/crepuscularity-dev",
    "crates/crepuscularity-cli",
    "crates/crepuscularity-reactive",
    "crates/crepuscularity-ssr",
    "crates/crepuscularity-tui",
    # GPUI desktop shell with embedded V8 runtime (build V8 on demand):

[profile.release]
lto = "fat"
codegen-units = 1
panic = "abort"
strip = "symbols"

# ABI / cdylib embedders: `cargo build -p crepuscularity-abi --profile abi`

inherits = "release"
panic = "abort"
codegen-units = 1



# PGO-optimised release — use via scripts/pgo-build.sh:

#
# Manual equivalent:

inherits = "release"

proc-macro2 = "1"
quote = "1"
syn = { version = "2", features = ["full", "extra-traits"] }
sha2 = "0.11"
toml = "1"
tracing = "0.1"
tracing-subscriber = { version = "0.3", features = ["env-filter"] }

axum = "0.8"
base64 = "0.22"
console = "0.16"
futures-util = "0.3"
http = "1"
indicatif = "0.18"
js-sys = "0.3"
notify = "8"
rayon = "1"

serde_json = "1"

# Crepuscularity

> **Stability:** This project is **unstable** and in active development. APIs, CLI flags, and template semantics may change without a semver-major release until **1.0**. Pin exact dependency versions and expect occasional breakage.

Think React Native turned into a systems UI toolkit: one compact `.crepus` language can drive GPUI desktop apps, Ratatui terminal UIs, Chromium/Firefox extensions, web output, native mobile shells, embedded panels, and LVGL Pro. Crepuscularity also ships hot reload, runtime rendering, and a GPUI desktop shell with an embedded V8 bridge for native capabilities.

Write UI in a concise, indentation-based template DSL (`.crepus` files). Templates compile at build time via the `view!` macro or render at runtime with full hot-reload support. The same `.crepus` syntax drives native desktop (GPUI), terminal UIs (Ratatui), browser extensions (MV3), HTML output, and React/JSX — and is the foundation for native mobile backends targeting SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose.

Use [Aurorality](https://github.com/tschk/aurorality) for united SwiftUI macOS + iOS apps.

## Why Crepuscularity

- **GPUI component workflow with hot reload** — live template updates without recompiling app code
- **Rust-owned MV3 extension target** — write popup, background, and content-script surfaces in `.crepus`, then emit Chromium or Firefox bundles without adopting a JavaScript framework or app bundler as the primary authoring model
- **One syntax, multiple backends** — the same template works across GPUI (native desktop), HTML, React/JSX, and browser extensions today; **`crepuscularity-native`** lowers `.crepus` to JSON **View IR** for SwiftUI / Jetpack Compose shells (see [`examples/native-shells`](examples/native-shells/README.md))
- **Polyglot plugin contract** — host languages consume View IR JSON through `crepus native ir` or the optional `crepuscularity-abi` C session API, then create UI from the typed node tree; drop-in reference packages and native workspace files live under [`plugins/`](plugins/README.md)
- **Terminal UIs without a second UI language** — **`crepuscularity-tui`** maps `.crepus` elements, includes, slots, control flow, and Tailwind-style terminal classes onto Ratatui frames
- **Embedded panels (in testing)** — **`crepuscularity-embedded`** renders `.crepus` into an RGB565 buffer you flush over SPI (**ILI9341**, **ST7789**) or into an **LTDC** framebuffer on STM32/ESP32; see [`docs/embedded.md`](docs/embedded.md) and [`examples/embedded-dashboard`](examples/embedded-dashboard/README.md)
- **Desktop shell for embedded guest apps** — **`crepuscularity-lite`** embeds V8 in a GPUI host with a Rust native-capability bridge, optional file watching, workers, plugin capabilities, and TypeScript/TSX guest transpilation
- **Compile-time and runtime paths** — `view!` macro for zero-overhead AOT compilation; `parse_template` / `render_nodes` for full runtime flexibility and hot reload

## Quick Start

```bash
# Install the CLI
cargo install --path crates/crepuscularity-cli

# If `crepus` is not found, Cargo still installed the binary under ~/.cargo/bin — add it to PATH,
# e.g. for zsh:  export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"
# (Rustup normally prepends this for login shells; some terminals omit it.)

# Create a new GPUI app
crepus init gpui my-app
cd my-app
SDKROOT=$(xcrun --show-sdk-path) cargo run

# Or create a browser extension
crepus init webext my-extension
cd my-extension
crepus build
# Load dist/unpacked/ in chrome://extensions
```

## Minimal target builds

Put every output in one `crepus.toml`, then run one command:

```toml
[[targets]]
type = "web"
id = "site"
site = "docs-site"
out = "docs-site/dist"
entry = "index.crepus"

out = "dist/panel.xml"
name = "Panel"
root = "screen"

[targets.vars]
device = "STM32F411"
```

```bash
crepus build
crepus build web
crepus build panel
crepus build --target panel
```

```

print()

for name, info in sorted(manifest.items()):
    externals = [d for d in info['deps'] if not d.startswith('crepuscularity') and d not in manifest]

# Crepuscularity

> **Stability:** This project is **unstable** and in active development. APIs, CLI flags, and template semantics may change without a semver-major release until **1.0**. Pin exact dependency versions and expect occasional breakage.

Think React Native turned into a systems UI toolkit: one compact `.crepus` language can drive GPUI desktop apps, Ratatui terminal UIs, Chromium/Firefox extensions, web output, native mobile shells, embedded panels, and LVGL Pro. Crepuscularity also ships hot reload, runtime rendering, and a GPUI desktop shell with an embedded V8 bridge for native capabilities.

Write UI in a concise, indentation-based template DSL (`.crepus` files). Templates compile at build time via the `view!` macro or render at runtime with full hot-reload support. The same `.crepus` syntax drives native desktop (GPUI), terminal UIs (Ratatui), browser extensions (MV3), HTML output, and React/JSX — and is the foundation for native mobile backends targeting SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose.

Use [Aurorality](https://github.com/tschk/aurorality) for united SwiftUI macOS + iOS apps.

## Why Crepuscularity

- **GPUI component workflow with hot reload** — live template updates without recompiling app code
- **Rust-owned MV3 extension target** — write popup, background, and content-script surfaces in `.crepus`, then emit Chromium or Firefox bundles without adopting a JavaScript framework or app bundler as the primary authoring model
- **One syntax, multiple backends** — the same template works across GPUI (native desktop), HTML, React/JSX, and browser extensions today; **`crepuscularity-native`** lowers `.crepus` to JSON **View IR** for SwiftUI / Jetpack Compose shells (see [`examples/native-shells`](examples/native-shells/README.md))
- **Polyglot plugin contract** — host languages consume View IR JSON through `crepus native ir` or the optional `crepuscularity-abi` C session API, then create UI from the typed node tree; drop-in reference packages and native workspace files live under [`plugins/`](plugins/README.md)
- **Terminal UIs without a second UI language** — **`crepuscularity-tui`** maps `.crepus` elements, includes, slots, control flow, and Tailwind-style terminal classes onto Ratatui frames
- **Embedded panels (in testing)** — **`crepuscularity-embedded`** renders `.crepus` into an RGB565 buffer you flush over SPI (**ILI9341**, **ST7789**) or into an **LTDC** framebuffer on STM32/ESP32; see [`docs/embedded.md`](docs/embedded.md) and [`examples/embedded-dashboard`](examples/embedded-dashboard/README.md)
- **Desktop shell for embedded guest apps** — **`crepuscularity-lite`** embeds V8 in a GPUI host with a Rust native-capability bridge, optional file watching, workers, plugin capabilities, and TypeScript/TSX guest transpilation
- **Compile-time and runtime paths** — `view!` macro for zero-overhead AOT compilation; `parse_template` / `render_nodes` for full runtime flexibility and hot reload

## Quick Start

```bash
# Install the CLI
cargo install --path crates/crepuscularity-cli

# If `crepus` is not found, Cargo still installed the binary under ~/.cargo/bin — add it to PATH,
# e.g. for zsh:  export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"
# (Rustup normally prepends this for login shells; some terminals omit it.)

# Create a new GPUI app
crepus init gpui my-app
cd my-app
SDKROOT=$(xcrun --show-sdk-path) cargo run

# Or create a browser extension
crepus init webext my-extension
cd my-extension
crepus build
# Load dist/unpacked/ in chrome://extensions
```

## Minimal target builds

Put every output in one `crepus.toml`, then run one command:

```toml
[[targets]]
type = "web"
id = "site"
site = "docs-site"
out = "docs-site/dist"
entry = "index.crepus"

[[targets]]
type = "lvgl"
id = "panel"
template = "ui.crepus"
out = "dist/panel.xml"
name = "Panel"
root = "screen"

[targets.vars]
device = "STM32F411"
```

```bash
crepus build
crepus build web
crepus build panel
crepus build --target panel
```

Rust build scripts can use the same manifest for render-output targets:

```rust
let artifacts = crepuscularity::target::write_manifest_file("crepus.toml")?;
```

### Published CVE/GHSA Records

**No published CVEs or GHSAs exist for any `crepuscularity-*` crate** on any queried source:

| Source | Query | Result |
|--------|-------|--------|
| NVD REST API (`keywordSearch=crepuscularity`) | `https://services.nvd.nist.gov/rest/json/cves/2.0?keywordSearch=crepuscularity` | 0 results |
| OSV (crates.io) | `crepuscularity`, `crepuscularity-core`, `crepuscularity-cli`, `crepuscularity-web`, `crepuscularity-webext`, `crepuscularity-ssr`, `crepuscularity-tui`, `crepuscularity-lite`, `crepuscularity-native`, `crepuscularity-embedded`, `crepuscularity-reactive`, `crepuscularity-runtime` | 0 results |
| GitHub Security Advisories | `repos/tschk/crepuscularity/security-advisories` | 0 results |
| GitHub Advisory DB | `advisories?query=crepuscularity` | 0 relevant results |

**Explanation**: Crepuscularity is an early-stage (pre-1.0, `v0.4.x`) project. Its crates are not yet published on crates.io or widely deployed, which means no CVE IDs have been requested for its vulnerabilities.

### Internal Security Fixes (git log — no CVE assigned)

Four security vulnerabilities were identified and fixed internally between 2 June and 16 June 2026. None received CVE/GHSA identifiers:

| # | Date | Component | Bug Class | Commit | Summary |
|---|------|-----------|-----------|--------|---------|
| 1 | 2026-06-02 | `crepuscularity-web` (SSR) | XSS (CWE-79) | `d1e2a794` | RawHtml rendering path used unsanitized inner HTML. Fixed by adding `ammonia::clean` to strip `<script>` and malicious tags. Unit tests added in `tests/ssr.rs`. |
| 2 | 2026-06-09 | `crepuscularity-cli` (dev server) | Path Traversal (CWE-22) | `643068e6` | The `/islands/` dev server handler allowed `..` traversal to read arbitrary files. Fixed by validating relative path resolution against the canonicalized base directory. |
| 3 | 2026-06-16 | `crepuscularity-cli` (config loader) | Path Traversal (CWE-22) | `73e24257` | Config relative path resolution for guest paths and prelude scripts allowed traversal outside the base directory. Fixed by canonicalizing paths and checking prefix match. |
| 4 | 2026-06-16 | `crepuscularity-webext` (content script) | XSS (CWE-79) | `eb668b23` | Content script created DOM nodes without sanitizing HTML. Fixed by adding `sanitizeHTML()` with DOMParser-based allowlist for tags and attributes, blocking `on*` event handlers and dangerous URL schemes. |

### Key Dependency Advisory Status

| Dependency | Version | Known Vulns | Notes |
|------------|---------|-------------|-------|
| `ammonia` | 4.1.2 | 4 past advisories (all fixed) | Latest version; RUSTSEC-2025-0071 (SVG/MathML mutation XSS) is fixed in 4.0.3+ |
| `hyper` | 1.10.1 | 14 historical advisories | Recent version, no active vulns at this version |
| `tokio` | 1.52.3 | 10 historical advisories | Latest stable; no active vulns |
| `axum` | 0.8.9 | 0 | Recent, well-maintained |
| `reqwest` | 0.12.28 | — | Recent |
| `v8` (rusty_v8) | 149.4.0 | V8 own CVEs apply | Embedded in `crepuscularity-lite` with the `v8` feature |
| `gpui` | 0.2.2 (pinned) | 0 | Pinned exact version due to API breakage |

## Dependency Intelligence

### Rust Runtime (crates.io ecosystem)

The workspace depends on 928 unique packages total. Key direct dependencies by category:

**Core infrastructure:**
- `crepuscularity-core` — parser, AST, expression evaluation (all crates depend on it)
- `serde` / `serde_json` — serialization
- `toml` — config parsing
- `sha2` — hashing (content IDs)
- `tracing` / `tracing-subscriber` — observability

**Web/Server:**
- `axum 0.8` — HTTP framework for SSR (`crepuscularity-ssr`)
- `tokio 1.52` — async runtime
- `hyper 1.10` — HTTP transport
- `reqwest 0.12` — HTTP client (in `crepuscularity-lite`)
- `ammonia 4.1` — HTML sanitizer (XSS protection)

**UI Runtimes (optional):**
- `gpui 0.2.2` — GPUI native desktop (pinned exact)
- `ratatui 0.30` — terminal UI (`crepuscularity-tui`)

**WASM/Browser:**
- `wasm-bindgen 0.2` / `js-sys` / `web-sys` — WASM bridge (`crepuscularity-web` `dom` feature, `crepuscularity-reactive`, `crepuscularity-webext`)
- `serde-wasm-bindgen` — WASM serialization

**Embedded JS:**
- `v8 149` / `oxc 0.128` — embedded V8 + TS/TSX transpiler (`crepuscularity-lite`, optional)
- `icu_calendar` / `icu_locale` — V8 ICU data

**Plugins (polyglot):**
- Plugin bindings shell out to `crepus native ir --stdin-json` via:
  - Python: `subprocess.run()` with user-controlled template paths
  - PHP: `proc_open()` / `exec()` with path from caller
  - Go: `exec.Command()` with path from caller
  - TypeScript/Bun: `spawnSync()` with path from caller
  - Ruby: `exec` / `Open3`
  - Zig: via V (self-built)
  - C/C++/C#/Kotlin/Swift/Java: via ABI

**Editors:**
- VSCode extension: `vscode-languageclient ^9.0.1` (TypeScript)

### Risk Assessment — Supply Chain

| Component | Risk | Rationale |
|-----------|------|-----------|
| `ammonia 4.1.2` | Low (monitor) | Past XSS vulns but current version clean; critical for SSR HTML safety |
| `v8 149` (rusty_v8) | Medium | Large attack surface; V8 CVEs periodically; only in `crepuscularity-lite` optional feature |
| `gpui 0.2.2` pinned | Low-Medium | Pinned exact version means no automatic patch updates for transitive vulns |
| Plugin subprocess calls | Medium | All plugins (`render_ir`) invoke `crepus native ir` with caller-controlled template path; no validation of path before passing to shell |
| `oxc 0.128` | Low | AST-based TS transpiler; new dependency |
| `tree-sitter-crepus` | Low | Language grammar; small surface |
